cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: RBAC namespace scoping means the Role and RoleBinding both live in one namespace, so the permissions only apply inside that namespace. It is how you give a user access to, for example, only the frontend namespace and not the whole cluster.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: The RBAC authorizer only checks RoleBindings in the namespace the request targets. For cluster-wide access or cluster-scoped resources like Nodes, use ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding. RBAC cannot restrict specific nodes, and SSH access to nodes is outside RBAC entirely; that needs OS, cloud IAM and network controls.

questions.q: Does a Role in default grant access in other namespaces?
questions.a: No. A Role and RoleBinding only apply in the namespace they are created in.

questions.q: When do you need a ClusterRole?
questions.a: When you need the same permissions in every namespace or access to cluster-scoped resources such as Nodes.

questions.q: Can Kubernetes RBAC control SSH access to nodes?
questions.a: No. SSH is outside Kubernetes. You need Linux users, SSH config, sudo policy, cloud IAM, bastions and firewalls.
